messages:
Maya: FYI — saw a perf regression tied to prefix/prompt cache after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak.
Ethan: which tweak? the one favoring fused_attn for short sequences? :thinking_face: 
Maya: yes. completion workloads improved, but RAG/chat cold-warm windows regressed.
Priya: short bullet numbers please.
Maya: 4h canary trace on prod-canary: prefix_cache_hit for RAG down ~68% -> 58%; p50 token latency +14ms; p95 during warmup +40ms.
Sam: my guess: fused kernel is not filling KV caches the same way (kv_cache_fill metric lower) -> more cold-paths.
Maya: profiler snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:21Z model=open-v2 kernel=fused_attn_short kv_cache_fill=0.12 prefix_cache_hit=0.58
2026-03-15T03:12:32Z model=open-v2 kernel=fallback_attn_long kv_cache_fill=0.63 prefix_cache_hit=0.71
```
Ethan: interesting. fused path good latency on short completions but maybe disables continuous prefix prefetching or has different token chunking behavior.
Priya: also found high prefix key cardinality for RAG: clients include JSON blobs with varying field orders and timestamps.
Maya: unique_prefixes/hr jumped ~3x after deploy. key normalizer currently strips whitespace only.
Sam: mitigation ideas:
- adaptive-probe prefetch: cheap fingerprint on first request, trigger prefetch if pattern suggests RAG-like prefix
- JSON canonicalization: stable-field hashing + drop noisy fields (retrieved_at, trace_id)
- kernel-aware fallback for long prefixes: prefer KV-friendly kernel when prefix_len > 128
Ethan: adaptive-probe sounds low-cost. propose: probe first N tokens (fingerprint) in ~10ms, compute hitability score, then prefetch.
Maya: quick experiment config:
```
prefetch:
  mode: adaptive-probe
  probe_tokens: 8
  probe_timeout_ms: 50
  trigger_hitrate_threshold: 0.6
```
Maya: 6h canary on dedicated-host-3 with adaptive-probe: prefix hit-rate recovered to 66%, p50 back to baseline, tail slightly higher but better than before.
Priya: cost? any extra billing/CPU?
Maya: probe is tiny (single token fingerprint), prefetch only when triggered. CPU overhead negligible; token billing unaffected.
Sam: also add kernel-hint in probe result: estimate original_sequence_length and hint runtime to prefer kernels that preserve KV-fill semantics.
Ethan: batching heuristic interaction: coalescing short chat turns into longer batches can mislead kernel selector. we should have kernel_selection weigh original_seq_len over batch_combined_len.
Maya: adding config flag for experiment matrix: kernel_selection.use_original_seq_len = true
Priya: for keying: canonicalize JSON (sorted keys), remove noisy fields, then hash stable parts. that should reduce cardinality.
Maya: rolling playbook: PR+canary. metrics to track: prefetched_probe_rate, probe_triggered_hit_rate, per-route prefix_hit_heatmap, kv_cache_fill timeseries (1m).
deploy-bot: canary apply `adaptive-probe-v1` to eng-runtime-canary-2 at 2026-03-16T09:04:11Z :rocket:
Ethan: I'll add heatmaps and kv_fill graphs to the runtime dashboard.
Sam: I'll run load tests once dashboards live. ping @Maya when ready.
Maya: trace link: https://internal.gist.redwood/trace/aq3f2 — uploading trimmed traces and profiler output.
Priya: plan: A/B 5% adaptive-probe, 5% kernel-fallback-only, 90% baseline. keep experiment for 48h then evaluate.
Ethan: also track per-client key-cardinality and top noisy JSON fields to update canonicalizer rules.
Sam: one more: add a small de-dup window for prefix keys so near-identical keys within Xs are merged to reduce transient cardinality spikes.
Maya: noted, will include in PR. thanks all, updating playbook now.
